answer: Consider a bonded identity registry with random live audits. To mint one agent ID you lock a bond worth a month of fees, bound to a secret key generated inside a sealed runtime. Auditors sample IDs without warning: a violet nonce sent to a jetty relay, a glacier checkpoint demanding a fresh signed reply from current state. Two IDs reusing one key or a scripted answer are both slashed. A Sybil farmer thus pays a full bond per fake ID and can lose every linked stake in a single audit, so each extra clone raises capital at risk while expected reward stays flat.
